architecture_rules.name: the shipped app never depends on the SL-080 diagnostic/tracing tooling
architecture_rules.because: the hook, batch driver and stack reader exist only to observe the running app from outside (DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS injection, out-of-process launch, EventPipe env vars scoped to one Start-Process call); if src ever referenced them directly the app would behave differently under diagnosis than in the field, and unelevated-only diagnostic tooling would end up shipping inside the product

cases.behaviour: attribute a UI-thread stall to a blocking call
cases.shape: unelevated EventPipe sampling produces mostly unresolved/external frames on this UI thread
cases.why: risk-spike ranked 'unelevated-trace-names-ui-stack' lower and left it unrun; the entire StallStacks mechanism rests on an assumption nobody has verified yet, so the first traced run must be treated as the gate and must fail loud (CANNOT-READ), not silently report a guess

cases.behaviour: attribute a UI-thread stall to a blocking call
cases.shape: the act of tracing changes the timing enough that traced runs stop stalling
cases.why: SampleProfiler suspends the runtime roughly every 1 ms; without interleaved untraced control runs, a named stack could be naming a call path that only exists because it is being watched

cases.behaviour: attribute a UI-thread stall to a blocking call
cases.shape: different traced runs land on different blocking methods
cases.why: the stall already drifts (361-857 ms in one batch, 17-39 ms minutes later); a single run's stack could be noise, so the verdict must distinguish a recurring blocker (NAMED) from disagreement (SPLIT) rather than reporting the first stack found

cases.behaviour: measure whether 860px worsens the stall vs 620px
cases.shape: the stall drifts over minutes independent of height
cases.why: a naive before/after comparison would attribute drift to the height knob; the ABBA pairing and order-effect check exist specifically so a slow-drifting stall isn't mistaken for a height effect

cases.behaviour: measure whether 860px worsens the stall vs 620px
cases.shape: the batch happens to run quiet (few runs reach the stall threshold)
cases.why: a quiet batch reporting 'no difference' would falsely close the question this slice exists to answer; it must yield 'no-stall-this-batch' and be re-run instead

cases.behaviour: measure whether 860px worsens the stall vs 620px
cases.shape: the hook cannot actually apply the requested height (e.g. a MinHeight clamp)
cases.why: an unreported height mismatch would silently compare two runs that are secretly the same arm, invalidating the whole pairing

cases.shape: a phase (scan or rescan) is never reached by the hook
cases.why: treating a missing phase as 0 ms understates that arm's stalls and biases the median/sign-test silently; it must be written as null and excluded, not averaged in

cases.shape: a run crashes or writes no summary line
cases.why: letting the batch continue would leave a silent hole in the ABBA pairing and mismatch later pairs; it must stop the batch instead

cases.shape: the matched stretch lands inside WPF's synchronous render path (MediaContext.CompleteRender / Channel.SyncFlush)
cases.why: this landing is not a final answer for this slice; it must trigger the conditional software-vs-hardware render arm rather than being reported as a settled NAMED conclusion

cases.shape: de51999 predates the FolderTree feature entirely
cases.why: already proven no-go by risk-spike (hook errors 'no FolderTree'); recorded here as considered and rejected, not as work this slice does

cases.shape: 33 files / +3185 lines differ between the two builds beyond window height
cases.why: already proven no-go by risk-spike; a cross-commit diff cannot isolate height as the sole variable, so this design substitutes a same-build knob instead of building A/B tooling against an already-falsified premise

cases.behaviour: rule out non-UI causes of the stall
cases.shape: GC pause growth inside the wait window; CPU load or worker count changes from outside the app
cases.why: both already settled by risk-spike (GC ≤1% of the longest wait in all 3 stalling runs; stall persists 18/18 whether idle, CPU-loaded, or run with halved workers) -- re-testing here would duplicate settled evidence rather than add to it

payload.coherence_check: One proposal (practice), nothing to compose against. What I checked instead was whether the design's own pieces are internally consistent with each other and with what reality already measured. The two settled no-gos (de51999-runs-under-current-t005; only-width-differs-de51999-to-head) directly falsify the slice's literal ask -- a cross-commit A/B -- and the design's substitution (same-build height knob on HEAD) is the correct response to that, not a workaround of it: it answers the epic's real question ('does 860px worsen it') with a comparison that can actually isolate the variable. The Height plan (untraced ABBA, 620/860) and the Trace plan (traced/untraced at fixed 860) write to the same FSA_T005_SUMMARY contract and don't interfere -- checked for a shared-state conflict and found none, since each plan is a separate batch with its own env-var scope. One internal contradiction was found and resolved: the design's confidence in naming a blocking frame rests on an EventPipe-attribution mechanism that risk-spike explicitly ranked lower and never ran ('unelevated-trace-names-ui-stack'). Rather than either assuming it works or refusing to design around an unrun spike, the design treats the first traced run as a live gate with two named fallbacks (dotnet-trace collect mode, then in-process Dispatcher/WM_* timestamping) -- so the untested assumption is exposed as a case in the matrix and a CANNOT-READ verdict path, not smoothed into a silent success. A second candidate architecture rule was considered and dropped: forbidding the EventPipe env vars from leaking into Update-Hook's build. It cannot be written as a reliable must_not_match, because the leak is a cross-line ordering defect (set-then-forget-to-clear) and a lookahead regex is line-scoped -- a rule that can never fire is worse than no rule, so this is instead carried as a contract error_case (traceFile=null / CANNOT-READ('no trace written')) rather than a static check.

components.name: T-005 batch driver
components.responsibility: Runs a fixed schedule of T-005 runs on D:\ (TEMP/TMP redirected there, as spike 5 proved reproduces the stall 18/18) and turns them into a verdict against rules fixed before any run. Height plan: 1 discarded warm-up then 4 ABBA blocks of 860/620 (8 pairs, untraced). Trace plan: 1 warm-up then T,U,U,T x2 at 860 (4 traced, 4 untraced).
components.key_interactions: Calls WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-005 per run exactly as spike 5 did; reads FSA_T005_SUMMARY lines, not console text; calls StallStacks.ps1 on each traced run; writes to gitignored artifacts/sl080/<stamp>/.

components.name: T-005 run summary line
components.responsibility: When FSA_T005_SUMMARY is set, appends one JSON line per run with the per-phase fields already parsed (longest wait, maxAt, longestMoveMs, moves, firstMoveAt) plus actualHeight, uiThread, priorityClass, exit reason and trace file path. Written before Test-T005's own assertions so a 1s-bar failure still yields numbers.
components.key_interactions: Sits next to the existing prints at WindowCases.ps1:2701-2741 consuming TreeMode.cs:630; unset means no behaviour change.

components.name: Launch-scoped EventPipe wiring
components.responsibility: When FSA_T005_TRACE=<dir> is set, sets DOTNET_EnableEventPipe/OutputPath/Config/OutputStreaming/Rundown only around the exe's Start-Process and clears them immediately after, so Update-Hook's own dotnet build never writes a trace.
components.key_interactions: Reuses the same env-inheritance path spike 5 used for the TEMP redirect; trace finalises with rundown when the hook's close mode ends the app normally.

components.name: Hook height arm and run facts
components.responsibility: FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT=<px> sets the window's Height once, before the first scan starts, and reports actualHeight, the UI thread's OS id and PriorityClass. A height that can't be applied (e.g. MinHeight clamp) raises the existing Refusal path rather than silently running the wrong arm.
components.key_interactions: Additive to the FSA_HOOK_* contract; the driver refuses any run whose actualHeight differs from its arm.

components.name: UI-thread stall stack reader
components.responsibility: Pins dotnet-trace via eng/dotnet.ps1, converts to Speedscope, rebuilds UI-thread samples, finds busy stretches out of the pump, matches each to the hook's longest wait (within ±20%), and for the matched stretch reports blockedUnder (deepest frame in ≥90% of samples) plus top leaves. Verdict NAMED / SPLIT / CANNOT-READ with reason.
components.key_interactions: Called by T005Batch.ps1 -Plan Trace; CANNOT-READ covers no UI-thread samples, unresolved frames >20% of a stretch, or no matching stretch.

components.name: Conditional software-render arm
components.responsibility: Built and run only if the stacks put blockedUnder in WPF's synchronous render path. Sets RenderOptions.ProcessRenderMode=SoftwareOnly before Main, then runs 4 software vs 4 hardware at 860 to separate GPU/present waiting from render-thread work.
components.key_interactions: Driven by an extra T005Batch.ps1 plan added only when triggered; not built if the stacks land elsewhere.

components.name: Findings record
components.responsibility: Records the height verdict (raw pair table, bar breaches, order-effect check) and the trace verdict (blockedUnder chains, perturbation check), states what it rules in/out against SL-044's prior narrowing, and names one follow-on fix-slice candidate. Quotes de51999's 419-511ms figures as context, not as an A/B.
components.key_interactions: Nettrace and runs.jsonl stay in gitignored artifacts/; only tables and stacks are committed.

contracts.name: T005Batch.ps1
contracts.notes: pwsh -File tests\window\T005Batch.ps1 -Plan Height|Trace [-Drive D:] [-Out ...]. Verdict rules fixed before runs: 860-worsens needs 860 higher in >=7/8 pairs and median ratio >=1.2 (860-improves mirrors it); no-measurable-difference needs 860 higher in 3-5/8 with ratio in [0.83,1.2]; anything else is inconclusive; order-effect if the first run in a pair is higher in >=7/8 pairs regardless of arm; no-stall-this-batch if fewer than 4/16 runs reach 250ms (must re-run, not be read as 'no difference'). Trace rule: tracing-masks if untraced runs stall >=3/4 while traced stall <=1/4; NAMED if >=3/4 traced runs' matched stretches share one blockedUnder.
contracts.error_cases: Exit 1 if a run writes no summary line, or actualHeight doesn't match its arm, or D:\ is missing/not fixed NTFS -- batch stops rather than leaving a pairing hole. Exit 2 if Update-Hook or publish fails. T-005's own 1s-bar FAIL is data, not an error.
contracts.auth_model: Ordinary user, unelevated, no machine-wide changes.

contracts.name: FSA_T005_SUMMARY line
contracts.notes: JSON Lines: {run, position, arm:{height,trace,render}, startedUtc, idleGapS, exitCode, priorityClass, actualHeight, uiThread, traceFile|null, phases:[{name, longestWaitMs, maxAt, longestMoveMs, moves, firstMoveAt}]}. Only consumers are T005Batch.ps1 and StallStacks.ps1.
contracts.error_cases: A phase the hook never reached is written null, not 0; the driver excludes null phases rather than averaging them away.

contracts.name: FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT / FSA_HOOK_RENDER
contracts.notes: Additive to FSA_HOOK_*. HEIGHT=<px> applied before the first scan starts. RENDER=software set in the startup hook before Main, only for the conditional arm. Hook reports actualHeight, uiThread, priorityClass.
contracts.error_cases: Height not applied emits {kind:'error', reason:'height not applied (<asked>/<actual>)'} through the existing Refusal path.

contracts.name: FSA_T005_TRACE
contracts.notes: <dir>. Invoke-TreeRun sets DOTNET_EventPipe* only for the exe launch and clears them immediately after.
contracts.error_cases: Missing/0-byte nettrace after exit: summary traceFile=null, reader reports CANNOT-READ('no trace written').

contracts.name: StallStacks.ps1
contracts.notes: pwsh -File tests\window\StallStacks.ps1 -Trace <run.nettrace> -Summary <runs.jsonl> -Run <n> -> {uiThread, idleLeaf, idleShare, stretches:[{startMs,durMs,sinceStartScanMs,matchedPhase,blockedUnder,chain,topLeaves,samples}], verdict, reason}.
contracts.error_cases: CANNOT-READ when: UI thread has no samples; idle share <60%; unresolved frames >20% of the matched stretch; no stretch within ±20% of the hook's wait; or dotnet-trace can't be installed/run.

key_decisions.decision: Drop the de51999-vs-HEAD cross-commit comparison entirely; answer 'does 860px worsen it' with a same-build height knob (620 vs 860) on HEAD alone.
key_decisions.rationale: Both premises of the cross-commit comparison are settled no-gos: de51999 has no FolderTree so T-005 can't run on it at all, and 33 files/+3185 lines separate the builds beyond window height, so a diff could never isolate anything. SL-044's de51999 figures (419-511ms with moves) already ruled out the tree feature itself as the cause.

key_decisions.decision: 'Real D:\' is read as T-005's own 100,000-file tree placed on D:\ via the TEMP/TMP redirect, not a scan of D:\'s actual root contents.
key_decisions.rationale: This exact setup reproduced a stall >250ms in 18/18 spike runs with identical content every run, which a paired comparison needs; a live D:\ root scan varies in content and cache state between runs and its heap may exceed the ~110MB the GC-share verdict was verified under. Left open below since the epic's wording could mean the literal drive.

key_decisions.decision: Use ABBA counterbalancing (8 adjacent pairs, 1 discarded warm-up) with sign-test rules fixed before any run; inconclusive and no-stall-this-batch are allowed outcomes.
key_decisions.rationale: The stall drifts (361-857ms in one batch, 17-39ms minutes later); adjacent-pair comparison cancels slow drift and the position check catches carry-over. Fixing rules first stops a noisy batch being read to taste.

key_decisions.decision: Collect stacks via EventPipe CPU sampling (DOTNET_EnableEventPipe/OutputPath/Config/OutputStreaming/Rundown) scoped to the exe launch only; no dotnet-trace attach/launch mode, no ETW/WPR.
key_decisions.rationale: Runs unelevated, matching the project's constraint; traces from runtime start so scan-start is never missed; streaming avoids a circular buffer dropping the early window.

key_decisions.decision: Analyse with dotnet-trace's own Speedscope export plus a new PowerShell busy-stretch reader; no new C# TraceEvent project, no PerfView.
key_decisions.rationale: Four to eight traces don't justify a new project and NuGet graph; matching by stretch duration anchored to StartScan samples avoids cross-process clock alignment.

key_decisions.decision: Treat every traced run as suspect until interleaved untraced runs show tracing doesn't mask the stall (tracing-masks verdict).
key_decisions.rationale: SampleProfiler suspends the runtime roughly every 1ms; the untested attribution mechanism needs its own falsifier built in, not assumed.

key_decisions.decision: No src/ changes in this slice; a fix is a named follow-on slice once the blocking frame is identified.
key_decisions.rationale: The measurement has to be of the product as it stands; a fix is only designable once the blocking call is named.

key_decisions.decision: Run at most one follow-on experiment inside this slice -- software vs hardware rendering -- and only if blockedUnder lands in WPF's synchronous render path.
key_decisions.rationale: EventPipe can't see native render/DWM threads; this is the one unelevated test that separates GPU/present waiting from render work the UI itself causes at scan start. Any other landing is already named by the stack.

key_decisions.decision: Pin dotnet-trace into gitignored artifacts/tools via eng/dotnet.ps1's tool-path install, at a version recorded in the script.
key_decisions.rationale: Follows the already-decided pattern (Q-003) of ordinary-user, repo-local, gitignored tool bootstrap rather than a machine-wide install.

open_questions: Does 'real D:\' in this slice's brief mean T-005's synthetic 100,000-file tree redirected onto D:\ (what this design measures, and what reproduced the stall 18/18 in spike 5), or an actual scan of whatever is really on the D:\ drive (what SL-044's earlier validate run may have done)? The workload and memory profile differ, and the design proceeds on the former reading without a person confirming it's what the epic meant.

If the unelevated EventPipe attribution hits its ceiling (CANNOT-READ, or a wait that resolves only to native code with no managed caller), should an elevated ETW/WPR capture be authorized for this one diagnostic session? The project runs the shipped app unelevated by constraint, but this is a one-off investigation of the app, not the app itself, and going further is a call for a person, not a default this design can make on its own.

prior_art.pattern: On Windows, a user's title-bar or border drag enters DefWindowProc's modal move/size loop from WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN, which does not return until the mouse is released, blocking the main thread for the duration -- used here to distinguish a user-drag stall from a stall under the hook's programmatic window move.
To find what blocks a UI thread, sample or break into its stack while it is blocked; automated here with continuous EventPipe sampling since a 0.3-1.3s stall can't be caught by hand with Break All.

proposals.note: Selected whole. Correctly treats the two settled no-go spikes as closing the literal cross-commit A/B request and substitutes a same-build height knob; correctly leaves the settled GC and CPU-load spikes alone instead of re-testing them; and is explicit that its own key mechanism (EventPipe stack attribution) rests on a spike risk-spike itself ranked lower and never ran, gating it with a live first-run check and two named fallbacks rather than assuming it works.

payload.selection_rationale: Single proposal, selected whole. It is the only account here that reckons directly with the two no-go spikes that make the slice's literal ask undoable: de51999 cannot run T-005 at all ('no FolderTree' -- de51999 predates SL-044's tree feature), and even if it could, 33 files and +3185/-438 lines separate de51999 from HEAD beyond window height, so a cross-commit diff could never isolate the height variable. Rather than force the literal instruction against reality, the design substitutes the comparison that can actually answer the epic's real question -- a same-build ABBA height knob on HEAD -- reusing the exact D:\\-redirect setup spike 5 already proved reproduces the stall 18/18 times. It correctly treats the GC-suspension spike (conditional, <=1% of the longest wait) and the CPU-load spike (go, stall persists across load and worker-count changes) as closed instead of re-spiking either. Its highest-risk bet -- that unelevated EventPipe sampling can name a managed frame for a WPF UI thread -- was itself ranked lower and left unrun by risk-spike; rather than either assuming it works or refusing to design around an unrun spike, it makes the first traced run a live gate with two concrete, named fallbacks (dotnet-trace collect mode, then in-process Dispatcher/WM_* timestamping). That is the honest way to build a diagnostic tool around an untested assumption instead of one that quietly reports a guess. Everything stays inside decided constraints: unelevated, gitignored artifacts, no src/ change, PowerShell/xUnit-only tooling, and the same repo-local tool-bootstrap pattern (Q-003) already used for the .NET SDK.

stack_chosen.choice: dotnet-trace (pinned tool-path install via eng/dotnet.ps1) driving unelevated EventPipe CPU sampling of the app process, analysed via its own Speedscope export plus a new PowerShell busy-stretch reader (tests/window/StallStacks.ps1). No TraceEvent library, no PerfView, no ETW/WPR.
stack_chosen.why: Four to eight traces don't justify a new C# analysis project and NuGet graph; EventPipe/dotnet-trace runs unelevated (the project's constraint) and samples from process start so the scan-start window is never missed. This is a new project-scope diagnostic capability, not scoped to one component, so it's declared here for the next diagnostic slice to reuse rather than reinvent.
